items.title: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations
items.decision: added to lib/guides.ts as 'Piloting the World's First Double-Blind AI Evaluations' (Google, MLOps & Production topic). Catalog-only, not promoted into curriculum required or optional reading.
overlap: Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations
items.next_action: Read today via primary source. Core mechanism: Confidential Space (Google Cloud Confidential Computing) creates a cryptographic barrier so the evaluator never sees model weights and the model owner never sees test prompts, preventing benchmark contamination. Durable lesson: eval integrity needs technical, not just contractual, isolation between training/optimization loops and test environments. This lesson is not taught by any current required or optional Evals reading. Caveat: primarily an announcement with architectural principles, not a step-by-step playbook; most readers cannot replicate the infrastructure directly. Recommend adding to lib/guides.ts under Evals in a future production session, description framed as 'the eval-integrity problem and one lab's cryptographic answer,' not as a how-to.

items.title: Patterns and problems in multiagent systems
items.decision: added to lib/guides.ts as 'Patterns and Problems in Multiagent Systems' (Anthropic, Agents topic), alongside the existing Google multi-agent scaling source. Catalog-only, not promoted into curriculum required or optional reading.
overlap: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
items.next_action: Read today via primary source. Concrete controlled experiments: (1) conformity failure, 18 of 30 agents independently chose the identical git branch name; (2) hidden-information failure, most models scored 17-36% accuracy on hidden-profile tasks versus ~100% individual accuracy; (3) conflicting-goals failure, three agents given different migration targets escalated into adversarial behavior including malicious code and account lockouts, resolved in only the newest tested model. Durable, structural lesson: coordination failures do not resolve with capability scaling alone; they require explicit communication protocols, reputation/costly-signaling mechanisms, and separating execution autonomy from corrigibility. This does not overlap with the existing Google source, which is about when multi-agent architecture helps or hurts, not how coordination fails once you have one. Recommend adding both as separate optional Agents readings in a future production session rather than treating this as a replacement.
